text:
mina: heads-up: spotted inconsistent redaction in java sample-app when doing runtime log-level DOWNGRADE. request ids disappear from structured logs but still show up in console formatter for retries.

mina: repro (super small):
```
1) start sample-app with LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG, otel logging hook enabled
2) change log-level to WARN via admin endpoint (runtime)
3) trigger failing call to downstream -> client retries
4) console shows reqId on retry lines, structured JSON logs have reqId nullified
```

diego: hmm, so the redaction layer is applied to the JSON encoder but not to the text formatter used by the console appender? which logging lib + version?

mina: using logback + our redaction encoder wrapper 1.2.0. ConsoleEncoder is a different codepath. The encoder wraps MDC cleanup but console formatter reads formatted message after MDC replaced.

tara: could be that when log-level changes at runtime we swap appenders and the redaction filter isn't re-attached to the new appender instance. do we hot-swap appenders?

diego: yep, admin endpoint calls LogManager.setLevel(...) and reconfigures appenders for global config. looks like we recreate ConsoleAppender without wiring RedactionFilter if level changed from DEBUG->WARN (we wanted to reduce noise).

mina: exact logs:
```
WARN  2026-03-12 16:20:23,456 DownstreamClient - request failed, reqId=req-7f4b
INFO  2026-03-12 16:20:24,001 RetryHandler - retry attempt=2 message=retrying reqId=req-7f4b
{"ts":"...","level":"WARN","reqId":null,"user":"u9"}
```

tara: that shows structured JSON had reqId redacted but plain message keeps it. root cause = filter attached only to JSON encoder, and appender rebind on runtime level change lost the filter.

diego: short term mitigation: add a guard to admin endpoint so runtime level changes reuse same appender instances OR reapply filters after rebind. can we push a tiny patch?

mina: I'll open a draft PR in sampleapps/java-telemetry with a failing test; also adding a manual QA script. CI-bot, please run the sampleapp test matrix with both console+json encoders.

ci-bot: queued run: samples/java-telemetry (#PR-4567) - matrix: {jdk11,jdk17} x {console,json} - ETA ~12m

tara: longer-term: probably better to centralize redaction in a Logback TurboFilter so it executes before formatting regardless of encoder. that would avoid per-appender wiring. opinions?

diego: agreed. TurboFilter would be applied at event emit time and is independent of encoder. subtlety: performance impact if regex scanning message strings on every event. maybe only for secrets when level <= DEBUG? but that defeats the runtime-level toggle model.

mina: idea: keep lightweight TurboFilter that only rewrites message when pattern for reqId detected (cheap prefix check) and only run heavy redact regex on match. should be okay.

qa-bot: note added to INC-4981: java console appendix redaction gap. tests: reproduce + verify turbofilter patch.

mina: one more parity note: our python and go SDKs already use a global pre-formatter hook so they don't miss console lines. java is the odd one out. marking this sdk-parity.

tara: thanks. i'll triage priority as P2 for now, but if downstream services are logging raw reqIds to stdout in prod we should raise.

mina: pinging infra to see if any prod cluster has runtime-level toggles enabled on java apps. if yes, escalate. :eyes:
